answer: Sybil defense in an agent economy rests on a per-identity bond locked in that identity's own vault. Each new key must lock fresh collateral, so N sock puppets tie up N units of a scarce asset. An attestation proves which key spoke, but the bond is what makes a fake identity costly, and its cipher signature binds the claim to that one stake. On a proven false claim the bond is slashed, and the sable mark of prior slashing is read by peers weighing new agents, so a mesa of fresh puppet keys is priced before it can act. Honest agents reclaim the bond; an attacker pays again per key.
